transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-09-30
Start time: 08:32 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Tran (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Northbridge Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Platform Eng), Ravi Narayan (Data Privacy)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync to review quality heatmap from last 2k evals, discuss prompt-batching experiments, and triage a small set of regression failures flagged in the scorer. Focus on guardrail false positives and a couple hallucination cases.

Topics:
- Heatmap walkthrough
- Scoring thresholds and false positive triage
- Prompt batching impact (latency vs token cost)
- Security / data residency questions
- Next steps and owners

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sophie Tran: Alright good morning everyone, um thanks for joining. I think we've got about 38 minutes today, we'll run through the heatmap that Diego sent and then dig into the top regressions. Maya, Ethan, thanks for carving time.
[00:12] Maya Patel: Yeah thanks Sophie, appreciate it. Quick note I'm dialing in from London so GMT+1, hoping we can keep it tight.
[00:20] Diego Alvarez: Cool, I'll share my screen — bear with me, the pdf had some weird rendering so I'm using the exported csv. Okay first slide, overall pass rate for the 2k sample is 86.2%, which is up 1.3% since last week, but there are concentrated failures on the 'financial-disclosure' prompt set.
[00:44] Ethan Cole: When you say pass rate, is that the score threshold at 0.7 right? Does that map to our production metric or the eval scorer? I thought our prod gating uses 0.75.
[00:56] Diego Alvarez: Good call — this export used 0.7 for higher recall so we can inspect more edge cases. We can easily rerun at 0.75 — I can include both in the next export.
[01:10] Maya Patel: I actually prefer 0.75 for production parity. But show us where the failures are.
[01:16] Diego Alvarez: Sure, on the heatmap the 'financial-disclosure' row shows concentrated red cells for intents 'sensitive-personal' and 'regulatory-advice' — that suggests the prompt is triggering guardrails too aggressively for a subset that looks like benign compliance questions.
[01:34] Ravi Narayan: Is this a guardrail false positive or model hallucination? Our privacy team is worried about over-blocking and losing utility.
[01:42] Diego Alvarez: Mostly false positives from the classifier that flags 'regulatory' keywords. The base model is giving reasonable completions but the filter upstream is catching them. We can tune the classifier threshold or add a lightweight rule-based exception list for known safe templates.
[01:58] Sophie Tran: Quick question on runtime impact — if we add a rule-based whitelist, what's the cost and latency hit? Any tradeoffs?
[02:06] Diego Alvarez: Rule checks are essentially negligible, a few ms. The main cost is complexity: maintaining templates. Alternatively, we can adjust the classifier threshold — that'll buy recall but may increase actual bad outputs. Tradeoff.
[02:22] Ethan Cole: On the prompt-batching tests, we saw a 12% token cost reduction when batching 4 prompts versus 1, but tail latency increased for some user flows. Numbers were from Hosted run; do we expect similar on Dedicated?
[02:38] Diego Alvarez: On Dedicated there's less variability — continuous batching implementation is optimized for reserved pools. In our internal tests Dedicated produced comparable cost savings with only ~3-5% median latency increase versus Hosted's 8-12% in tail. But this depends on request size and KV cache hit rates.
[02:58] Maya Patel: So is the recommendation to run prefix caching + batch size 3 on Dedicated for higher throughput? Our latency SLO is 300ms P95.
[03:08] Diego Alvarez: For your request sizes and 300ms P95, we recommend batch size 2 with prefix caching first. Batch size 3 can push P95 close to threshold depending on prompt lengths. We should run a quick regression on your 500 sample to validate.
[03:24] Sophie Tran: Action: Diego will run a 2k regression comparing Hosted vs Dedicated on the curated 500 sample + extra 1.5k from logs. Deliverable is latency/cost delta spreadsheet.
[03:36] Diego Alvarez: Yep noted.
[03:38] [04:00] (background noise, brief overlap)
[04:10] Ethan Cole: Security — Ravi had questions about KMS integration and audit logs, I didn't want to interrupt the quality part but it's priority for our legal team.
[04:22] Ravi Narayan: Yeah, two items: do you store any PII in the hosted logs? And can we integrate with our customer-managed KMS for key rotation?
[04:32] Sophie Tran: Short answer: logs can be redacted and we support customer-provided KMS for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer encryption at rest and we can present the SOC2 + encryption appendix. I'll follow up with the tailored notes.
[04:44] Diego Alvarez: Also note that Dedicated has optional no-logs mode for KV cache, and Private/VPC gives you full control over KMS. But if you want hosted with CMK that's available for enterprise plans, we should document the options.
[05:00] Maya Patel: We also had a couple hallucination cases in the 'claims' prompt set — responses inventing regulatory frameworks. Any quick mitigation strategies?
[05:10] Diego Alvarez: For hallucinations, the short term is guardrail post-processing (e.g., cite-only mode, require sources), or reranking with a conservative model. Long term, curriculum fine-tune or RLHF on those prompts.
[05:24] Ethan Cole: Reranking might be expensive — what's the unit cost tradeoff?
[05:28] Diego Alvarez: It depends on model sizes; reranking with a small model is often cost-effective compared to running a large safety model. We can estimate based on token counts on the sample.
[05:36] Maya Patel: On the heatmap, can you highlight the top 5 regression example rows? We want to annotate them with labels to send to our domain SMEs.
[05:44] Diego Alvarez: Yep I'll include the csv with the top 5 examples, plus context, prompt ID, and the model output. NOTE: some of the outputs got truncated in the export — the transcript might read 'Redwood Dedicate' in one place — apologies for the transcriber.
[05:58] Sophie Tran: haha transcription aside, the important part: we need reproducible failing cases. If you can provide 500 labelled examples by Friday that will speed up triage.
[06:10] Maya Patel: We can do 500, but can you also provide a script to map our internal prompt ids to the sample ids? That was messy last time.
[06:18] Diego Alvarez: Yep I'll attach the mapping script. It's a small python notebook, should run locally.
[06:24] Ethan Cole: Network question — our infra team needs to know whether peering or private link is better for latency. Any guidance?
[06:32] Diego Alvarez: Private link / VPC peering reduces egress variability. For critical low-latency workloads we recommend dedicated peering in the region or Dedicated deployment inside your VPC.
[06:44] Ravi Narayan: Also confirm data residency — logs for Hosted are stored in region X (EU), but our compliance team wants log storage in EU only.
[06:54] Sophie Tran: We'll confirm region; for Hosted you can select EU region and we can restrict retention. For Private you have full control. I'll include retention options in the security notes.
[07:06] Maya Patel: Back to guardrails — can we create a whitelist for certain known-customer templates to reduce false positives? That seems low risk.
[07:14] Diego Alvarez: Yes, whitelist at the classifier layer is straightforward. We'll need your SME to sign off on templates.
[07:20] Sophie Tran: Ok let's talk timelines: Maya, you said you can provide 500 prompts by 2025-10-03. Diego will run regressions and provide comparison by 2025-10-07. Sophie to send security appendix by 2025-10-01. We should aim to reconvene the week of 2025-10-13 for a focused remediation session.
[07:36] Maya Patel: That works, also can we get a heatmap export that includes both 0.7 and 0.75 thresholds so we can pick the gating threshold more empirically?
[07:46] Diego Alvarez: Absolutely.
[07:48] Ethan Cole: One small ask — could you include a quick note on how batching affects token accounting for billing? Our finance team is picky.
[07:56] Sophie Tran: Yes we'll include an amortized token-cost breakdown for batching scenarios.
[08:04] Diego Alvarez: Last quick technical note: some regression failures correlate with cold KV cache — for batched requests with diverse prefixes we lose cache hits. If you can add more warmup traffic or use pinned contexts it helps.
[08:20] Maya Patel: Noted. We'll try a pinning approach in our next run.
[08:24] Sophie Tran: Any blockers or outstanding asks before we close?
[08:28] Ravi Narayan: None from legal beyond that security appendix.
[08:30] Maya Patel: No blockers.
[08:32] Sophie Tran: Great — recap of next steps, I'll put them in the meeting notes and follow up with calendar invites for the week of 2025-10-13 for remediation. Thanks everyone.
